_doc: Field-wide milestones for the timeline (course-specific events live in each course.json). year < 0 means BC. area is one of: general, physical, inorganic, organic, analytical, biological, materials.

milestones.title: Boyle dissolves the alchemical elements
milestones.detail: The Sceptical Chymist attacks the Aristotelian and Paracelsian element doctrines as useless for explaining real experiments, and proposes instead that matter consists of corpuscles whose arrangements define what we call an element — the practical, operational idea that chemistry has used ever since.

milestones.title: Black isolates a gas and discovers latent heat
milestones.detail: Joseph Black shows that 'fixed air' (carbon dioxide) is a distinct substance held in magnesia and released by acids, the first of the elastic fluids to be pinned down as a chemical individual, and his measurements of heat absorbed in melting introduce the idea that energy hides in changes of state.

milestones.title: Lavoisier founds modern chemistry
milestones.detail: The Traité élémentaire de chimie sets the balance at the centre of the science: combustion is combination with oxygen, mass is conserved through every change, and a rewritten nomenclature makes compounds speak their composition — the overthrow of phlogiston in a single book.

milestones.title: Proust's law of definite proportions
milestones.detail: Analysing copper carbonates from mines and from the artificial malachite of the laboratory, Joseph Proust insists that a compound always contains the same elements in the same mass ratios, whatever its source — composition is fixed, and therefore atoms are thinkable.

milestones.title: Dalton's atomic theory
milestones.detail: John Dalton explains the laws of definite and multiple proportions by supposing that each element is a cloud of identical indivisible atoms and that compounds are small whole-number assemblies of them — the first quantitative theory of the invisible, and the beginning of stoichiometry.

milestones.title: Avogadro distinguishes atoms from molecules
milestones.detail: Amedeo Avogadro proposes that equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of particles, and that those particles may be molecules of two or more atoms — the distinction that would take fifty years to be accepted but without which atomic weights stay contradictory.

milestones.title: Wöhler makes urea from ammonium cyanate
milestones.detail: Heating an inorganic salt, Friedrich Wöhler crystallises urea, a compound long associated with living bodies — the first striking demonstration that organic compounds obey ordinary chemical laws and can be made in the flask, a watershed for the chemistry of life.

milestones.title: Spectrum analysis finds elements in sunlight
milestones.detail: Gustav Kirchhoff and Robert Bunsen show that each element emits and absorbs its own pattern of spectral lines, and use it to discover caesium and rubidium; within a decade the method finds thallium, indium and helium, and turns the solar spectrum into a chemical analysis.

milestones.title: Kekulé proposes the ring of benzene
milestones.detail: August Kekulé puts the six carbons of benzene in a closed chain with alternating single and double bonds, solving the strange compactness of aromatic chemistry and opening the vast coal-tar dye industry that made German chemical supremacy later in the century.

milestones.title: Mendeleev orders the elements
milestones.detail: Dmitri Mendeleev arranges the known elements by atomic weight and recurring valence, and — crucially — leaves gaps and predicts the properties of the missing ones; the discoveries of gallium, scandium and germanium turn a table into a law of nature.

milestones.title: The carbon atom is given a shape
milestones.detail: Jacobus van 't Hoff and, independently, Joseph Le Bel place carbon's four bonds at the corners of a tetrahedron, so that mirror-image molecules become inevitable and optical isomerism in tartaric acid finally makes sense — stereochemistry, and with it molecular handedness in biology, is born.

milestones.title: Gibbs invents chemical thermodynamics
milestones.detail: Working almost unnoticed in New Haven, Josiah Willard Gibbs shows that the direction and limit of every chemical change follow from a single function, later called the free energy, and his phase rule connects the states of a system to its components — equilibrium becomes a calculable thing.

milestones.title: Arrhenius lets salts fall apart in water
milestones.detail: Svante Arrhenius proposes that electrolytes dissociate into ions in solution — the reason salt water conducts — and his later equation for the temperature dependence of reaction rates becomes the working tool of every kineticist; the ionic theory wins him chemistry's first Nobel Prize.

milestones.title: van 't Hoff gives solutions their laws
milestones.detail: In his Études de dynamique chimique Jacobus van 't Hoff shows that dilute solutions obey the same pressure laws as gases, ties osmotic pressure to molecular weight, and applies thermodynamics to equilibrium and reaction rate — physical chemistry appears as a discipline with its own journal.

milestones.title: Werner explains the coordination compounds
milestones.detail: Alfred Werner proposes that metal atoms carry a fixed coordination number with bonds directed in space, so that cobalt ammines are understood as compact ions with ligands at the corners of octahedra — the foundation of coordination chemistry and of molecular geometry at metals.

milestones.title: The Curies isolate radium
milestones.detail: Working in a shed with tonnes of pitchblende residue, Marie and Pierre Curie concentrate and measure their way to decigram quantities of radium, proving a new element by its radioactivity — and inventing the patient, quantitative radiochemistry that would follow.

milestones.title: Grignard puts magnesium between carbon and halogen
milestones.detail: Victor Grignard's organomagnesium halides add to carbonyl groups with a selectivity no one had matched, making carbon–carbon bond construction a routine operation; the reagent class that bears his name remains the most used in the synthesis of alcohols and fine chemicals.

milestones.title: Haber fixes nitrogen from the air
milestones.detail: Fritz Haber demonstrates the catalytic synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen at high pressure and temperature, and BASF's engineers scale it up within four years — a high-pressure catalytic process that now feeds half the world and reshaped the nitrogen cycle of the planet.

milestones.title: Aston weighs the isotopes
milestones.detail: Francis Aston's focusing mass spectrograph separates ions by mass-to-charge with unprecedented resolution, showing that the elements are mixtures of isotopes of definite mass — the mass spectrometer becomes chemistry's scale for the invisible.

milestones.title: Bragg diffracts X-rays off crystals
milestones.detail: William Henry Bragg and William Lawrence Bragg turn Max von Laue's diffraction photographs into a method, nλ = 2d sin θ, and solve the structures of NaCl, diamond and the sulfides — for the first time the arrangement of atoms in a solid is measured, not imagined.

milestones.title: The chemical bond meets quantum mechanics
milestones.detail: Walter Heitler and Fritz London apply the new wave mechanics to H₂ and show that the bond is the lowering of electronic energy when two electron spins pair across the nuclei — valence bond theory, followed within two years by Hund, Mulliken and the molecular orbital method.

milestones.title: Fleming's mould and the antibiotic era
milestones.detail: Alexander Fleming notices that a contaminating Penicillium kills the staphylococci on his plates; a decade later Howard Florey and Ernst Chain purify the penicillins and prove them in patients, launching both antibiotic medicine and the era of structure-guided natural-product chemistry.

milestones.title: Uranium is split
milestones.detail: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann find barium among the products of neutron-bombarded uranium; Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch interpret it as the nucleus splitting in two, releasing enormous energy — chemistry and nuclear physics become inseparable, for medicine, power and weapons.

milestones.title: Pauling writes the bond into words
milestones.detail: The Nature of the Chemical Bond assembles hybridisation, resonance, electronegativity and bond energy into one quantitative picture of how molecules hold together; its scale of electronegativities and its habit of reasoning with orbitals still organise every textbook.

milestones.title: Martin and Synge invent partition chromatography
milestones.detail: Archer Martin and Richard Synge separate amino acids by letting them partition between two liquid phases, one held on a support — a counter-current method that becomes column and gas chromatography, and the workhorse separation of every laboratory that measures mixtures.

milestones.title: Nuclear magnetic resonance is observed
milestones.detail: Felix Bloch and, independently, Edward Purcell detect the precession of nuclear spins in a magnetic field; within twenty years chemical shift and coupling turn NMR into the principal method for determining molecular structure, and later into medical imaging.

milestones.title: Ferrocene breaks the sandwich
milestones.detail: Peter L. Pauson and Thomas J. Kealy make a startlingly stable orange compound from cyclopentadiene and iron; the sandwich structure proposed independently by Wilkinson, Fischer and by Rice and Ruff settles it, and organometallic chemistry of the transition metals opens as a central field.

milestones.title: The structure of DNA
milestones.detail: James Watson and Francis Crick build the double helix from Rosalind Franklin's and Maurice Wilkins's X-ray diffraction patterns and Chargaff's base ratios — two hydrogen-bonded chains whose copying mechanism is written in the structure itself, and chemical biology acquires its central fact.

milestones.title: Ziegler and Natta tame the olefins
milestones.detail: Karl Ziegler's titanium–aluminium catalysts polymerise ethylene at ordinary pressure, and Giulio Natta extends them to stereoregular polypropylene — coordination polymerisation begins, giving the plastics that dominate the modern material world and a Nobel Prize in 1963.

milestones.title: Orbital symmetry rules pericyclic reactions
milestones.detail: Robert Burns Woodward and Roald Hoffmann show that whether a thermal or photochemical cycloaddition or electrocyclisation is allowed follows from the symmetry of the orbitals that move — a qualitative theory that lets chemists plan stereospecific reactions on paper.

milestones.title: Merrifield builds peptides on a bead
milestones.detail: Robert Merrifield anchors the growing chain to an insoluble resin and drives each coupling to completion by washing away the excess reagent — solid-phase synthesis automates peptides and, later, oligonucleotides, making sequence-defined molecules a routine supply item.

milestones.title: C₆₀: a third form of carbon
milestones.detail: Kroto, Curl, Smalley and co-workers find a remarkably stable C₆₀ cluster in their laser-vaporised graphite, and the buckminsterfullerene cage is confirmed by bulk synthesis in 1990 — nanotubes, fullerenes and the whole nanocarbon field follow from that 720 amu peak.

milestones.title: Green chemistry writes its twelve principles
milestones.detail: Paul Anastas and John Warner set out twelve principles — prevention, atom economy, safer solvents, design for degradation, catalysis over stoichiometric reagents — turning an attitude of reducing harm into a checkable design methodology now embedded in industrial and academic practice.
